newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-MCGEECHAN PROMISES POSITIVE, DYNAMIC RUGBY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MCGEECHAN PROMISES POSITIVE, DYNAMIC RUGBY.

text.p: British Lions coach Ian McGeechan promised on Monday a positive, fluent and dynamic style of rugby from his side during their tour of South Africa.

"We've got to be flexible and dynamic. Obviously the set-piece is still very important because you need ball to play with, but we are prepared to play dynamically and, on occasions, to play with controlled risk," McGeechan said after the Lions' first training session at Durban's Kings Park.

"What we want in our squad is a group of players who are open-minded with what is possible. We would never discourage the players ever from being positive. You've got to stay flexible and I don't want them (the players) to feel they're in a strait-jacket.

"Yet, to play flexible rugby, you have to adopt a more disciplined approach, the players have to be more self-disciplined in everything they do. I've never been an advocate of loose rugby but of instinctive rugby."
The 35-man playing squad trained for two hours during the morning in typically hot Durban weather, reaching 27 degrees Celsius.
"It was probably a good start for us in the sense that it can't really get hotter for us out here," McGeechan said.

"Our first training session was more of a getting-to-know-one-another session, but there was a fair bit of discomfort as well. We'll be looking to increase the level of intensity at further sessions right through this week.
"We know we've got to play and train with a lot of intensity. Today was to make sure that we're all on the same wavelength."
McGeechan said there had been a few minor injury worries.

England fly-half Paul Grayson has a slight muscle strain after the extra kicking practice he has put in over the past three weeks, Irish lock Jeremy Davidson suffered a knock during training and Scottish centre Alan Tait has a thyroid problem.
"But both Jeremy and Alan will be fine although Paul is probably out of contention for our first game in Port Elizabeth this Saturday," McGeechan said.
McGeechan and his assistant coach Jim Telfer then spent lunch with South African referees' committee members Freek Burger and Steve Strydom to iron out possible areas of different interpretation.

"We wanted to talk with them to understand which areas South African referees see as important and we then have to adjust to that. I think it's being realistic, we have to be comfortable and it would be crazy not to prepare for it.
"The last thing we want is a string of penalties against us in our tour matches -- that wouldn't be doing us any good and it wouldn't be doing the game any good."
The Lions play their first tour match against an Eastern Province invitation side in Port Elizabeth on Saturday.
